column1: # examples/inventory.csv — an inventory file (docs/OPERATIONS.md).
# A line whose first byte is # is a comment
# first data line is the header: each column is found under the name the
# [inventory-source.mappings] table of the configuration gives it
# (examples/config.toml), so a site keeps its own headers. RFC 4180 quoting:
# a cell that holds the delimiter is quoted ("access
# name                the device's name
# management_address  the address karvi connects to (IPv4 or IPv6)
#                     resolves through DNS on the client when this is blank
# platform            a built-in platform or a [platform.NAME] alias of the
#                     configuration (c9300 below)
#                     platform-resolution.default
# transport           system (OpenSSH) or native (scrapligo-v1)
#                     mode's default
# site, groups        selectors for credential rows and policy maps
#                     are separated by
# session_cap         at most this many sessions to the device at once
# credkeyref          pins the device to the credential CSV row whose credkey
#                     equals it (examples/credentials.csv)
# owner               a free attribute, kept in the records as attributes.owner
name,management_address,platform,transport,site,groups,session_cap,credkeyref,owner
edge-01,192.0.2.10,cisco_iosxe,system,nyc,"access
edge-02,192.0.2.11,cisco_iosxe,system,nyc,"access
# the core pair runs on the native transport and pins the break-glass row
core-01,2001:db8::10,cisco_iosxe,native,iad,"core
# an alias platform of examples/config.toml: IOS XE with one paging command
access-09,192.0.2.19,c9300,system,nyc,"access
lab-linux-01,192.0.2.50,linux,system,lab,"test
